record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.context_brief: Hamiltonian circuits in embedded segment visibility graphs
record.original_question: Does every segment visibility graph contain a Hamiltonian cycle that becomes a non-self-intersecting Hamiltonian circuit in the embedded segment visibility graph?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8 Every segment visibility graph G contains a Hamiltonian cycle C that corresponds to a Hamiltonian circuit in the embedded segment visibility graph G′.

Later, Conjectures 8 was proved for all classes of segments in S by Hoffmann and Tóth [65] using the result of Bose et al. [15], and they presented an O(n log n) time algorithm for locating a Hamiltonian circuit in G′.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let S = {s_1, …, s_n} be a finite set of pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane in general position (no three endpoints collinear). The segment visibility graph G(S) is the graph whose vertex set consists of the 2n endpoints of the segments of S, and whose edges are: (i) the n segments of S themselves, and (ii) all pairs of endpoints {p, q} (belonging to possibly different segments) such that the open segment pq does not cross any segment of S, i.e. p and q are mutually visible. The embedded segment visibility graph G'(S) is the straight-line drawing of G(S) in which every vertex is placed at its corresponding endpoint and every edge is drawn as the straight-line segment between its endpoints.

A Hamiltonian cycle of G(S) is called non-self-intersecting (in the embedding) if, when its edges are drawn as straight-line segments in G'(S), no two of those edges cross.

Prove or disprove: For every such finite set S of pairwise disjoint segments in general position, the segment visibility graph G(S) admits a Hamiltonian cycle that is non-self-intersecting in the embedded graph G'(S).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture was resolved affirmatively by Hoffmann and Tóth, who proved that every segment visibility graph contains a non-crossing Hamiltonian cycle in its straight-line embedding, and gave an O(n log n) algorithm to construct it (building on results of Bose, Houle, and Toussaint on disjoint-compatible geometric matchings/spanning structures).
